Jerslev parish, Børglum herred · baptism of Christen, 13 February 1698

Finding Fredenborg

A cottage called Fredenborg stood in Svennum, Jerslev parish, from before 1676 until some time after 1884. Court books, the 1688 and 1844 land registers, the parish register and three generations of cadastral maps agree on where. This page is its map and its history.

Where the evidence sits

Fredenborg house, ±15 m Godparent’s home 1676 court record Register place, same page Context

Background: a Google Maps satellite screenshot, georeferenced by fitting 28 labelled towns and the Trøgdrupvej pin to their OpenStreetMap coordinates. Fit error is about 9 px RMS, 21 px worst case, which is roughly 100 to 230 m on the ground. The imagery is Google’s and is here for private research use. Parish outlines are modern (DAGI, simplified) and sit close to the 1698 boundaries. Farms recorded only as a surviving road name are placed on that road. The two Trøgdrup villages are placed from Trøgdrupvej and Klausholm and are approximate. No distance on this page comes from a document; all are measured between modern coordinates. Hover a point for its evidence. The ring around Fredenborg reaches the Jerslev village fields where the 1676 tithe grain was taken; the dashed line is the journey to the Trøgdrup common.

The house, pinned: 57.2806 N, 10.1207 E

Best estimate of the Fredenborg house site is 57.28060, 10.12073, with an uncertainty of about 15 m. It is the north side of the Hellumvej 23 farmyard, 9740 Jerslev, about 25 m north of the present farmhouse, where the yard’s outbuildings stand today. The farmhouse itself occupies the site of the 1884 “10a” house.

StepSourceWhat it gives
1676Jerslev herred court bookAnders and Peder Andersen “i Fredenborg”; the household harvests a strip on Jerslev mark.
1688Christian V’s matrikel, modelbog 1781, fol. 112–114Svennum Bye no. 8: Niels Andersen, Huus, owner Johan Kaas, hartkorn 0:1:0:1:1.
1688–1699Jerslev burial register“Peder Andersens barn i Fredenborg i Svennum”; Peder, Hans and Niels Andersen at the house, and from 1698 Søren Jensen; the byname “Niels Fredenborg”.
1813Original 1 cadastral sheet, Jerslev By sheet 2Svennum plot No 9, Ole Nielsen, house on the north side of the village street just north-east of No 10’s house.
1844Matrikel for Børglum Herred, Jerslev sogn fol. 395–397New no. 9, Ole Nielsen, old hartkorn 0 tdr 1 skp 0 fjk 1 alb — the unique match to 1688 no. 8. Old no. 9 (0-0-1-1) became new no. 10.
1884Original 2 cadastral sheet, “Svennum Bys Jorder”, redrawn 1884 from the 1806 surveyPlot 9a with its house drawn on the north edge of the common, 30 m east and 55 m north of the 10a notch house. Two features on this sheet survive: the pond by 8a and the three-winged farm west of the common.
1884General Staff 1:20,000 sheet “Jerslev”A building north of the smithy cluster at the lane end, in the same relation.
todayMatriklen (Dataforsyningen) and OpenStreetMapThe 1884 ditch is the garden pond at Hellumvej 23; the farmhouse stands on the 10a house site; the 9a site is the north side of the same yard. Parcel 15 on Hellumvej is the remnant of the common; 9b survives as a 2 ha field to the north-east.

How the point was placed: the 1884 General Staff 1:20,000 sheet “Jerslev” was triangulated from the national survey network, so unlike the cadastral sheets it needs no local anchor. It was positioned from its own neat lines and the published sheet footprint, then checked in Google Earth against the lidar contours, the roads and the ravine west of the village, all of which coincide. On it, two buildings stand north of the road by the smithy: a large one with a garden tree and a small one 50 m to its south-west, the same pair the 1884 cadastral sheet labels 9a and 10a. The small one falls 15 m from the present Hellumvej 23 farmhouse; the sheet’s blue ditch falls 11 m from the pond in that farm’s garden; the large one is Fredenborg. Two earlier placements, one anchored on the assumption that the farmhouse was the 10a house without rotation, the other on the pond and the Egelundsvej 3 farm, were 30 m and 95 m off and have been withdrawn. Google Maps: 57.28060, 10.12073.

The documents and maps behind the pin

Found: Fredenborg lay in Svennum

The Jerslev burial register, read from 1685 to 1700, names the house and its people. The decisive line is the first.

DateEntry (normalised)What it tells us
15 Jan 1688A child named Niels, Peder Andersen’s, i Fredenborg i SvennumFredenborg is in Svennum. Peder Andersen, summoned in 1676, still lives there.
11 Sep 1688Niels Andersen’s nameless child, i SvennumA second Andersen in Svennum.
26 Sep 1689Maren Nielsdatter, Niels Andersen’s wife, i Svennum, 36Niels Andersen widowed at Svennum.
1 Dec 1689Christen, Hans Andersen’s son, i Fredenborg, 9A third Andersen at the house.
6 Jan 1692Johanne, Niels Fredenborg’s child, i Jerslev, 7 weeksThe house name used as a byname.
31 Jul 1698Anders, Niels Andersen’s son, udj Svennum, 5 monthsA grandson named Anders.
26 Dec 1698Anna, Niels Fredenborg’s daughter, 9Same byname, ten years on.
7 May 1699Niels Tomsen Fredenborren, 80An old man of the house, born c. 1619; relationship unknown.
10 Sep 1702Jens, son of “Søren Jensen Fredenborg”, is baptised. The father’s patronymic, missing in 1698, is written here, and the house name is attached to him as a byname. Godparents from Sterup and Jerslev; Dorthe Jensdatter of the clerk’s house again.Jerslev baptisms
28 Jun 1704“Palli Nielsen i Fredenborg” stands godfather to a Jerslev child. A third household name at the house: Palle Nielsen, possibly a son of Niels Andersen’s neighbour Niels Tomsen, or a son-in-law.Jerslev baptisms
1708Niels Sørensen, 40, buried 15 Jan; a Søren Jensen “i Knæppen i Svennum” baptises a son Jens on 25 Nov. Knæppen is a locality in Svennum, so this may be the same Søren Jensen under a new address, or a second man of the name.Jerslev burials and baptisms
1716Anders Nielsen “i Svennum”, 65, buried 19 Jan.Jerslev burials
25 Dec 1719Niels Andersen “i Jerslef”, 82, buried, and the same day his wife Helle Jensdatter, 55. Born c. 1637, the right age for the Niels Andersen of the 1688 matrikel; by 1719 he had moved from Svennum to Jerslev village.Jerslev burials
17 Mar 1720Peder Sørensen “i Svennum”, 49, buried. Born c. 1671, so a Søren’s son of the right generation, perhaps Søren Jensen’s eldest.Jerslev burials
1720–1724Niels Jensen in Svennum, 50 (Dec 1720); Anders Jensen of Svennum, 19 (Jun 1722); Jens Andersen’s son of Svennum (May 1723); Jens Nielsen in Svennum, 78 (May 1724). The house name itself does not recur in the burials to 1725.Jerslev burials

Together with the 1676 court entries (Anders and Peder Andersen of Fredenborg) and the 1698 baptism (Søren of Fredenborg), the house held a family of Andersens for at least a generation: Peder, Hans, Niels and probably Søren, sons of an Anders. The Anders Pedersen who served as Kølskegård’s agent in Jerslev from 1632 to 1654 remains the likeliest father, unproven. Svennum sits 1.5 km from the church inside the tithe disc, 3.3 km from Kølskegård, and on the Jerslev side of the parish: every independent constraint on the map is satisfied. The Sønder Trøgdrup reading is closed; the 1676 summons recorded a Svennum man with an interest in Trøgdrup common, not a resident.

Svennum in 1813. The Original 1 cadastral sheet (surveyed 1813, Jerslev–Klæstrup–Svennum sheet 2) shows Svennum as a street village along “Svennum Gade” with about ten farms, matrikel 1–10 and 12, and four or five small house plots, matrikel 11, 13, 14 and 15, strung along the street. Tenants named on the sheet include Peder Pedersen (6), Chresten Olesen (5A), Ole Nielsen and Chresten Thomsen (9), Chresten Nielsen (10), Niels Jensen (12), Peder Jensen Bak (8), Niels Svendsen (3) and a Bundgaard (1). No plot carries the name Fredenborg. The house is one of these fifteen holdings; the 1688 matrikel for Svennum, which lists each holding with its tenant in Fredenborg’s own decade, is the document that would say which.

Svennum in 1688. Christian V’s matrikel, modelbog for Jerslev herred (Rtk. 312, vol. 1781, folios 112–114), lists Svennum Bye as ten holdings. Hartkorn is the 1688 (new matrikel) total for each holding, in tønder : skæpper : fjerdingkar : album, followed by a fifth remainder figure the surveyors used below the album. Rows with a single value are read from the first figure of the totals line; some second figures remain uncertain.

No.Tenant 1688TypeOwner (left margin)Hartkorn 1688 (new matrikel)Note
1Jens LaursenfarmHr. Otte … Vallø (reading uncertain)5:7:1:0:1Largest farm in the village; old matrikel 6:0:2:0.
2Niels Tomsensmall farmJohan Kaas0:5:0:0:3Very probably the “Niels Tomsen Fredenborren” buried 1699 aged 80.
3Niels Andersenfarm“Skolen” (school land; first word uncertain)3:4:3:1:2One of two Niels Andersens.
4Jens AndersenfarmJohan Kaas1:5:0:2:2A fourth Andersen brother, not yet seen in the register.
5Lars Nielsenfarmuncertain3:6:0:1:0Possibly the godparent Lars Nielsen of 1698.
6Mickel Christensen, Jens Nielsen, Steen Pedersen, Jens Sørensenfarm, 4 tenantsuncertain4:5:2:1:2
7Søren JensenfarmJohan Kaas3:1:1:0:1

Reading. Peder and Hans Andersen, both “i Fredenborg” in the register, hold nothing in 1688, so they lived in a brother’s holding. Niels Andersen holds two: a farm (no. 3) and a house (no. 8). A named house that sheltered several brothers’ families fits no. 8, the house, and “Niels Fredenborg” in the register is then the Niels Andersen of no. 8. The owner is Johan Kaas. The Kaas family owned Kølskegård; Anders Pedersen of Jerslev had been the Kaas family’s estate agent from 1632 to 1654, and Knud Kampmann, godfather in 1698, lived at Kølskegård. The circle is closed. The 1688 numbers do not carry into the 1813 map; the bridge is the 1844 matrikel protocol for Svennum, which records each new number’s old hartkorn. The entry whose pre-1844 hartkorn is 0 tdr 1 skp 0 fjk 1 alb is the modern plot.

Two words checked and set aside: the 1690 and 1695 entries “i Forbedringen” are a locality at Klæstrup, not Fredenborg. Source: Jerslev sogn kirkebog 1684–, burials, images 14415940–14415948 on Danish Family Search.

A history of Fredenborg

Everything below is from the records read in this study. Items marked hypothesis are inferences, not documented facts.

WhenWhat happenedSource
1632–1654Anders Pedersen of Jerslev, son of Peder Pedersen, acts in court for the Kaas family who own Kølskegård and most of Svennum. Hypothesis: he is the father of the Andersen brothers later at Fredenborg.Jerslev herred court books
1650s–1660sThe name Fredenborg, “peace-castle”, is probably given. It is absent from the court books of 1631–1650 and appears by 1676; the wars with Sweden ended in 1660.Inference
31 Aug 1676The priest’s farmhand comes to collect the tithe on Kirsten Jensdatter’s field on Jerslev mark. Anders of Fredenborg drives him off with a wagon stake and that night carts the grain home, 1.6 km to Svennum.Court book, 31 Aug 1676
7 Sep 1676Peder Andersen of Fredenborg is summoned, with Christen Mortensen of Klausholm and Peder Andersen of Allerup, to hear witnesses about the Bløden common between Nørre and Sønder Trøgdrup, 10 km to the south. Summonses “for vidne” went to everyone the testimony might bind, so he had a stake in that common; the herredsting had no jury, cases were heard by the herredsfoged with eight sworn men.Court book, 7 Sep 1676
19 Oct 1676Judgment: Anders of Fredenborg must prove title to the grain or face prosecution. He was claiming the crop as his own, so his household farmed that strip.Court book, 19 Oct 1676
1685Kirsten Jensdatter, mother of Jens Madsen of Jerslev, is buried: very probably the widow whose field it was.Jerslev burials, 24 May 1685
15 Jan 1688A child Niels, Peder Andersen’s, “i Fredenborg i Svennum”, is buried. The line that places the house.Jerslev burials
1688Christian V’s matrikel: Svennum no. 8, a Huus, tenant Niels Andersen, owner Johan Kaas, hartkorn 0:1:0:1:1. Niels also holds farm no. 3; a Jens Andersen holds farm no. 4; Niels Tomsen holds no. 2 next door.Modelbog 1781, fol. 112–114
1688–1689Niels Andersen loses a nameless child (Sep 1688) and his wife Maren Nielsdatter, 36 (Sep 1689), both “i Svennum”. Hans Andersen’s son Christen, 9, dies “i Fredenborg” (Dec 1689). Three brothers’ families are living at or beside the house.Jerslev burials
6 Jan 1692“Niels Fredenborg” buries a daughter Johanne, seven weeks old. The house name has become his byname.Jerslev burials
13 Feb 1698Christen, son of Søren of Fredenborg, is baptised at Jerslev church. Godparents: Knud Kampmann of Kølskegård, Kield Andersøn, Lars Nielsen (very likely the Lars Nielsen farming Svennum no. 5), Marie Fischer the priest’s wife, and Dorthe Jensdatter. The father is Søren Jensen (named in full in 1702), so not an Andersen brother; he probably came into the house by marriage to an Andersen daughter.Jerslev baptisms
31 Jul 1698Niels Andersen buries a son Anders, five months old, in Svennum: a grandson named for the old man.Jerslev burials
26 Dec 1698Anna, Niels Fredenborg’s daughter, 9, is buried.Jerslev burials
7 May 1699Niels Tomsen “Fredenborren”, 80, is buried: the neighbour on no. 2, born about 1619, who carried the house’s name.Jerslev burials
1725–1812Not yet read. The Jerslev registers continue; the Kaas estate papers and the Børglum-Jerslev court books after 1688 would carry the tenants’ names.—
1806–1813Enclosure survey. The house stands in plot No 9, owner Ole Nielsen (Chresten Thomsen struck out), on the north side of Svennum Gade; the house in the notch of No 10 is its nearest neighbour.Original 1, Jerslev By sheet 2
1844New matrikel no. 9, owner Ole Nielsen, old hartkorn 0-1-0-1 — the 1688 house, unchanged in assessment for 156 years.Matrikel for Børglum Herred, fol. 395–397
1884The house is still drawn on plot 9a in the redrawn cadastral map, and the General Staff survey shows a building there, north of the smithy.Original 2; General Staff sheet “Jerslev”
1884–1955Some time in this period the house is pulled down and the 9a plot is absorbed into the field now numbered 5l. Plot 9b, two hectares of No 9’s old strips, survives 400 m to the north-east.Original 2 validity; modern cadastre
todayThe north side of the Hellumvej 23 farmyard, 25 m north of the farmhouse: 57.28060 N, 10.12073 E, ±15 m.This study
